# FDG5129

> DO name elements of a named tuple using PascalCase, as if they were properties.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 5.9 Using Tuples in Member Signatures.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG5129
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application none, test none
- Language: [C# 7+] (before that: Before C# 7.0 there are no named tuples; name the properties of a descriptive type in PascalCase.)
- Status: draft

Message: Name the tuple element '{0}' in the signature of '{1}' in PascalCase

Library only: see FDG5127. FDG5129 reports each element name of a tuple in the signature of an externally visible method, constructor, delegate, operator, property, indexer or field that does not start with an uppercase letter. The rest of PascalCase is not checked. Overrides and interface implementations are not reported. Callers read the elements by name, so renaming them breaks their source and the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.

## From the book

Named tuples in C# allow access to their elements via the same syntax as accessing a property or field on a descriptive type, so they should be named accordingly.
